# Parks Near Us

Parks, trails and beaches across Sonoma County, each with something to look for and a question to wonder about together. Checked November 2, 2026.

## Santa Rosa

- [Spring Lake Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/spring-lake-regional-park), Santa Rosa. A calm lake ringed by paved paths, with birds to watch and frogs to listen for. Look for turtles stacked on the logs, sharing a warm spot. The ducks have their heads under the water and their tails in the air, so what might they be looking for down there? *Regional park, Lake, Birds, Stroller friendly, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Trione-Annadel State Park](https://parks.ca.gov/?page_id=31891), Santa Rosa. A big, wild park behind Spring Lake with rocky trails, Lake Ilsanjo and fields of wildflowers in spring. Look for buttercups, lupine and poppies on the rocky slopes. What might it feel like to be a fish in Lake Ilsanjo, looking up at the hikers on the shore? *State park, Lake, Wildflowers, Restrooms, Fee.*
- [Taylor Mountain Regional Park and Preserve](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/taylor-mountain-regional-park-and-preserve), Santa Rosa. Hills, grassland and wide views over the city, with trails that climb and little shade. Look for cows grazing and watch how they wrap their tongues around the grass. A hawk circles high above without flapping its wings, so how does it stay up so still? *Regional park, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Hood Mountain Regional Park and Preserve](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/hood-mountain-regional-park-and-preserve), Santa Rosa. A steep, rugged park of rocks, chaparral and big valley views, best for a long climb. Look for madrone trees, with smooth reddish bark peeling in curls. Why might the madrone shed its bark? *Regional park, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [North Sonoma Mountain Regional Park and Preserve](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/north-sonoma-mountain-regional-park-and-preserve), Santa Rosa. A steady climb through shady oak and bay forest into sunny meadows that fill with wildflowers in spring. Crush a fallen bay leaf gently and smell it. Some parts of the forest are dark and damp and some are sunny and dry, so which plants choose the shade, and which choose the sun? *Regional park, Wildflowers, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Matanzas Creek Trail](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Matanzas+Creek+Trail+Santa+Rosa), Santa Rosa. A flat, paved path along Matanzas Creek through city neighborhoods, good for strollers, bikes and scooters. Watch for a snowy egret standing still in the water. Plants and vines grow over the creek's concrete walls, so how did those seeds find a home in the middle of the city? *Trail, Birds, Stroller friendly, Free.*
- [Santa Rosa Creek Trail](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/santa-rosa-creek-trail), Santa Rosa. A paved path that follows Santa Rosa Creek across the city, shared with walkers and fast bikes. In fall and winter, look for toyon covered in red berries for the birds. So many people pass by walking, biking and pushing strollers, so where might everyone be going? *Trail, Stroller friendly, Free.*
- [Colgan Creek Trail](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/colgan-creek-trail), Santa Rosa. A quiet, flat neighborhood path in southwest Santa Rosa, good for a first bike ride, with spring wildflowers and birds in the tall grass. Listen for the red-winged blackbird's song before you see him. Sparrows and blackbirds both live along the creek, so do they all eat the same seeds? *Trail, Birds, Stroller friendly, Free.*
- [Joe Rodota Trail](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/joe-rodota-trail), Santa Rosa to Sebastopol. A long, flat, paved trail on an old railroad line, passing neighborhoods, fields and wetlands. Near the Sebastopol end, look for egrets, ducks and herons in the Laguna. Trains once ran on this very spot, so what might riders have seen from their windows? *Trail, Birds, Free.*
- [Kawana Springs](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Kawana+Springs+Santa+Rosa), Santa Rosa. A short, hilly loop trail on a quiet grassy hill tucked behind a neighborhood. In spring, look for small yellow flowers in the grass. It is so quiet here, so how many animals might be resting in the tall grass or in burrows underground? *City park, Trail, Wildflowers, Free.*
- [Andy's Unity Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/andys-unity-park), Santa Rosa. A neighborhood park with a colorful playground, a skate park, a community garden and a green lawn. Visit the garden and see how many vegetables and flowers you can name. With skating, swinging, gardening and talking all around, which spot is the busiest, and which is the quietest? *Regional park, Playground, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Bayer Neighborhood Park and Gardens](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Bayer+Neighborhood+Park+and+Gardens+Santa+Rosa), Santa Rosa. A community park with a playground, a community garden and a paved path for walking. Look for solar panels over the parking area. What might the panels be doing with the sunshine right now? *City park, Playground, Restrooms, Free.*

## North County

- [Foothill Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/foothill-regional-park), Windsor. Shady oak woodland with flat and hilly trails and soft, earthy paths. Listen for acorn woodpeckers and look for trees drilled full of holes and acorns. Acorn caps cover the ground but few acorns, so who is collecting all that food? *Regional park, Birds, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Riverfront Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/riverfront-regional-park), Windsor. A flat, easy park beside the Russian River, with lakes made from old gravel pits and tall trees that love water. Watch for a great blue heron standing still at the water's edge. Some trees have white, flaky bark and some have dark, shaggy bark, so why might they be so different? *Regional park, Lake, River, Birds, Stroller friendly, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Shiloh Ranch Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/shiloh-ranch-regional-park), Windsor. Trails climb through oak woods and grassy meadows to a ridge with big valley views, with little shade on the open paths. In fall and winter, look for toyon with bright red berries. The air feels cooler the moment we step into the shade, so how do the trees do that? *Regional park, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Cloverdale River Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/cloverdale-river-park), Cloverdale. A peaceful, flat park on the Russian River at the north end of the county, with trees, a boat launch and room for a picnic. Be quiet and you might spot river otters near the banks. The river moves slowly today, so how fast might it run in winter, full of rain? *Regional park, River, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Healdsburg Veterans Memorial Beach](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/healdsburg-veterans-memorial-beach), Healdsburg. A sunny summer beach on the Russian River, with shady picnic spots under the trees. Look up at the tall trees that shade the picnic area. Here the river is an open swimming beach, and at other parks it is wild and fast, so how many different moods does the river have? *Regional park, River, Beach, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Del Rio Woods](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/del-rio-woods), Healdsburg. A shady park on the Russian River with tall redwood, fir and oak trees, a beach and a gentle trail. Look for redwood sorrel, a clover-shaped plant carpeting the forest floor. Redwood bark is deep and stringy and bay bark is smooth and gray, so why might they be so different? *Regional park, River, Redwoods, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Russian River beaches](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Russian+River+beaches+Russian+River+area), Russian River area. Small access points along the Russian River, often with a little beach or a place to launch a canoe. Look for dragonflies with shiny bodies and clear wings hunting near the water. How many little beaches line the river, and how many could we visit in one day? *River, Beach, Free.*

## West County and Coast

- [Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve](https://parks.ca.gov/?page_id=450), Guerneville. A quiet grove of giant redwoods with soft, flat paths and cool air that smells of damp earth and bay. Look on the damp forest floor for a banana slug at work. It is so quiet in here, so what might the giant trees be doing to the wind and the sounds outside? *State park, Redwoods, Stroller friendly, Restrooms, Fee.*
- [Doran Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/doran-regional-park), Bodega Bay. A long, sandy strip between the calm waters of Bodega Harbor and the open Pacific, often windy. Look for sand dollars on the beach, and leave them for others to find. The ocean foam is bright white and full of bubbles, so what makes all those bubbles? *Regional park, Beach, Coast, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Gualala Point Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/gualala-point-regional-park), Gualala. A windy, wild place where the Gualala River meets the ocean, with smooth, white driftwood on the beach. Look for harbor seals resting on the sandy spit, and stay far away and quiet. The waves here are dangerous, so watch them from far back. How long does a piece of wood spend in the ocean to become so smooth and white? *Regional park, Beach, Coast, River, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Ragle Ranch Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/ragle-ranch-regional-park), Sebastopol. A gentle park of open fields and big, shady oaks, with flat paths for a slow walk, a picnic or a kite. Look for old oak trunks drilled full of holes where acorn woodpeckers store acorns. How do the woodpeckers remember which hole holds which acorn? *Regional park, Birds, Playground, Stroller friendly, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Stillwater Cove Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/stillwater-cove-regional-park), Jenner. A small, protected cove of pebbles and tide pools below the cliffs, with trails through redwood and fir forest above. At low tide, look gently under the seaweed for tiny crabs, anemones and sea stars. What tiny creatures might be waiting in these rock puddles? *Regional park, Coast, Tide pools, Redwoods, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Bodega Bay Trail](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/learn/planning-projects/project-directory/all-active-projects/bodega-bay-bike-and-pedestrian-trail/background), Bodega Bay. A flat, paved path along Bodega Harbor with views of the water, the fishing boats and the hills, often windy. Look closely at the gulls and see how many kinds you can find. The harbor is very still and the ocean beyond is wild, so what makes the harbor so calm? *Trail, Coast, Birds, Stroller friendly, Free.*
- [Pinnacle Gulch Coastal Access Trail](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/pinnacle-gulch-coastal-access-trail), Bodega Bay. A short, steep trail down a small valley to a beach with rock formations and tide pools, best at low tide. Look for sea anemones in the tide pools. The big flat rock on the beach has a crack down the middle, so what might have split it? *Regional park, Trail, Beach, Tide pools, Free.*
- [Shell Beach](https://parks.ca.gov/?page_id=451), Jenner. A small beach in Sonoma Coast State Park known for its tide pools, best at low tide. Look for sea anemones, sea stars and hermit crabs, and look with your eyes first. When the tide goes out, what is it like for the creatures left behind in their little pools? *State park, Beach, Coast, Tide pools, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Shorttail Gulch Coastal Access Trail](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/shorttail-gulch-coastal-access-trail), Bodega Bay. A small, steep trail down to a quiet beach at the north end of Salmon Creek beach. Look for gull feathers in the sand and see how they are made. The sand here is soft and deep, so why is the sand on some beaches firm and on others soft? *Regional park, Trail, Beach, Free.*
- [Spud Point Marina](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/spud-point-marina), Bodega Bay. A working marina, home to the Bodega Bay fishing fleet, with boats, gulls and salty air. Watch the fishing boats come in and see what they unload. Every boat has its own name, so who gets to choose a boat's name? *Regional park, Coast, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Sea Ranch Coastal Access Trails](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/sea-ranch-coastal-access-trails), The Sea Ranch. Trails that lead past private land to public beaches on the wild, open coast. Be respectful as you walk past homes. Look for cypress trees shaped by the wind. The cypress trees here are bent and twisted, so what might have shaped them? *Regional park, Trail, Coast, Beach, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Timber Cove](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Timber+Cove+Jenner), Jenner. A small, rocky cove on the coast with a boat launch and room for a picnic. After a storm, look for thick, brown kelp washed into the cove and feel how leathery it is. A tall sculpture stands on the cliff above the cove, so what might the artist have been thinking about? *Coast, Beach, Free.*
- [Forestville River Access](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/forestville-river-access), Forestville. A quiet path down to a sandy spot on the Russian River. Look for western pond turtles warming on a fallen log. If we drop a leaf in the slow water here, how far might it float? *Regional park, River, Beach, Free.*
- [Laguna de Santa Rosa Trail](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/laguna-de-santa-rosa-trail), Sebastopol. A flat, easy trail into a wetland that is one of the best places in the county to watch birds. Look for cattails, where birds love to hide. Trees grow right in the still, dark water, so what is it like to be a tree with its roots in water all the time? *Regional park, Trail, Birds, Stroller friendly, Free.*
- [Steelhead Beach Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/steelhead-beach-regional-park), Forestville. A long, sandy beach on the Russian River with a boat launch, surrounded by tall trees. Look for driftwood the winter floods piled up, and see what shapes you find. The river is wide and slow here, so how deep might it be? *Regional park, River, Beach, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Sunset Beach River Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/sunset-beach-river-park), Forestville. A wide summer beach on the Russian River with a seasonal swimming area. Look for dragonflies and their smaller, thinner relatives, the damselflies, zooming over the water. How is a summer dam built in the middle of a river, and where does the water go when it meets the dam? *Regional park, River, Beach, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [West County Regional Trail](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/west-county-regional-trail), Sebastopol to Forestville. A flat, paved trail through farms, orchards and vineyards, away from the cars. Look for apple trees, white with flowers in spring and full of apples in fall. The trail is flat and straight while the roads nearby curve over the hills, so why might that be? *Regional park, Trail, Stroller friendly, Free.*
- [Guerneville River Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/guerneville-river-park), Guerneville. A small park with a boat launch and a beach on the Russian River, right in town. Watch kayaks and canoes launch and paddle quietly away. How long might it take to float from here all the way to the ocean? *Regional park, River, Beach, Free.*
- [Maddux Ranch Regional Park](https://www.sonomacounty.com/outdoor-activities/maddux-ranch-regional-park/), Santa Rosa. Protected land in the hills, open on guided visits. Check the park's page before you go. Look up for large birds riding the high winds. What might it be like to be a bobcat walking these trails at night? *Regional park.*
- [Carrington Coast Ranch](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/learn/planning-projects/project-directory/all-active-projects/carrington-coast-ranch-regional-park-and-open-space-preserve), Bodega Bay. Protected coastal land of rolling hills, coastal scrub and ocean views, open on guided visits. Check the park's page before you go. Look for low, tough coastal plants such as coyote brush, and smell their leaves. Why might the bushes here grow so low? *Regional park, Coast.*
- [Monte Rio Beach](https://www.mrrpd.org/monte-rio-beach), Monte Rio. A big, sunny summer beach on the Russian River beside a historic bridge. Look for the smooth, colorful pebbles in the water. The big bridge has arches, so why might it have been built that way? *River, Beach, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Fort Ross State Historic Park](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=449), Jenner. A wooden stockade on the foggy coastal cliffs, where Russian settlers lived alongside Kashaya Pomo people about two hundred years ago. Look for the wooden chapel with its round dome and bell tower. What might it have been like to sail in a wooden ship all the way to this foggy, windy coast? *State park, Coast, Restrooms, Fee.*
- [Salt Point State Park](https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=453), Jenner. A large, wild park of rocky cliffs, hidden coves, tide pools, forest and grassy hills. Be careful on the rocks near the water. Look for honeycomb patterns in the sandstone, full of holes and grooves. How can soft water carve holes in hard rock? *State park, Coast, Tide pools, Restrooms, Fee.*
- [Sonoma Coast State Park](https://parks.ca.gov/?page_id=451), Bodega Bay to Jenner. A long string of beaches and cliffs, including Bodega Dunes and Salmon Creek Beach. The ocean here is dangerous, so stay well back from the waves. Look for sea stacks, the tall rocks standing alone in the ocean. The sand here is a different color than at Doran, so might it be made from different rocks? *State park, Coast, Beach, Restrooms, Fee.*

## South County and Valley

- [Sonoma Valley Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/sonoma-valley-regional-park), Glen Ellen. A gentle park with a wide, flat, paved trail, rolling hills and grand old valley oaks. Look for the valley oaks, huge and wide, with deeply lobed leaves that drop in winter. Some oaks here are huge and some are small and scrubby, so why might they grow in different places? *Regional park, Stroller friendly, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Tolay Lake Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/tolay-lake-regional-park), Petaluma. Wide, open hills and a seasonal lake in a place that has long been a gathering place for native peoples. There is little shade, so bring water. Look for tule reeds growing in the low, wet spots. What might this place have looked and sounded like long ago? *Regional park, Lake, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Crane Creek Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/crane-creek-regional-park), Rohnert Park. Rolling grassland and shady oaks with a loop trail, known for bright wildflowers in spring. Look for poppies, lupine and buttercups. The grass on the hills is tall and wavy, so what tiny animals might be hiding in it? *Regional park, Wildflowers, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Helen Putnam Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/helen-putnam-regional-park), Petaluma. Rolling hills and oak forest with wide, easy trails, big views and a pond at the bottom. Be very quiet and look for western pond turtles on the logs. What might be hiding just under the pond's still surface? *Regional park, Lake, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
- [Maxwell Farms Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/maxwell-farms-regional-park), Sonoma. A community park with big trees, open lawns, playgrounds and paths beside Sonoma Creek. Look down from a bridge for small fish in the creek. So many kinds of trees grow here, so who might have planted them? *Regional park, Playground, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Sugarloaf Ridge State Park](https://parks.ca.gov/?page_id=481), Kenwood. A big, wild park following Sonoma Creek into the Mayacamas Mountains, with redwood groves, oak woodland and Bald Mountain. On the Canyon Trail, look for the creek as a tiny stream splashing over rocks. What might it be like to stand on Bald Mountain above the fog, looking down on the clouds? *State park, Redwoods, Restrooms, Fee.*
- [Jack London State Historic Park](https://parks.ca.gov/?page_id=478), Glen Ellen. The ranch of the writer Jack London, with a museum, old farm buildings and shady trails. Look for the stone walls of the Wolf House ruins in the forest. Did Jack London find his story ideas walking these same trails? *State park, Restrooms, Fee.*
- [Bartholomew Park](https://www.sonomacity.org/contacts/bartholomew-park), Sonoma. A park in the hills east of Sonoma. Check the park's page before you go. Look around and see what the people here are doing together. What do you notice that you would like to come back and see again? *City park, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Hudeman Slough Boat Launch](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/play/boating-and-paddling/boat-launches), Sonoma. A flat, watery wetland (slough) connected to the bay, mostly a place to launch a boat or kayak. Watch for harbor seals' round heads popping up in the water. The water is moving with no waves, so is the tide coming in or going out? *Regional park, Birds, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Kenwood Plaza Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/kenwood-plaza-park), Kenwood. A small town park in the middle of Kenwood with a green lawn, a gazebo and a playground. Have a picnic near the gazebo. What does it feel like to be in the center of the town? *Regional park, Playground, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Larson Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/larson-park), Sonoma. An active park with ball fields and a playground. Watch the games and the play around you. Which part of the park is the busiest today? *Regional park, Playground, Restrooms, Free.*
- [McCormick Ranch](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=McCormick+Ranch+Kenwood), Kenwood. Protected land in the Mayacamas Mountains, open only on special guided visits. Look in soft dirt for animal tracks. What animals might be watching us from a hidden spot in the trees? *Trail.*
- [Penngrove Park](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Penngrove+Park+Penngrove), Penngrove. The main park in the small town of Penngrove, with a playground and a shady grove of trees. Look for the tall trees and smell a fallen leaf. How many picnics and parties might have happened in this park? *City park, Playground, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Petaluma Adobe State Historic Park](https://parks.ca.gov/?page_id=474), Petaluma. A large, two-story adobe building from the 1830s, made of mud and straw bricks. Look closely at the walls and the big, tan adobe bricks. What might it have been like to live and work here long before cars or electricity? *State park, Restrooms, Fee.*
- [Petaluma River](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Petaluma+River+Petaluma), Petaluma. Access points along the Petaluma River, a tidal waterway that connects the city to San Pablo Bay. Look for pelicans resting on the docks. What might it have been like to ride a steamboat up this narrow river? *River, Birds, Free.*
- [Shaw Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/shaw-park), Kenwood. A community park with a playground and a path along Kenwood Creek. Look at the creek, dry and rocky in summer and rushing in winter. What song can we make at the playground? *Regional park, Playground, Restrooms, Free.*
- [Ernie Smith Community Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/Visit/Ernie-Smith-Community-Park), Sonoma. A neighborhood park with a playground. Look for a little free library box. Who might leave the books, and who might take them? *Regional park, Playground, Free.*

# Parks Near Us

Parks, trails and beaches across Sonoma County, each with something to look for and a question to wonder about together. Checked November 2, 2026.

## Santa Rosa

- [Spring Lake Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/spring-lake-regional-park), Santa Rosa. A calm lake ringed by paved paths, with birds to watch and frogs to listen for. Look for turtles stacked on the logs, sharing a warm spot. The ducks have their heads under the water and their tails in the air, so what might they be looking for down there? *Regional park, Lake, Birds, Stroller friendly, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
  - **A bit about the park.** This is a park of water and sky. It is a hub of activity, with paths full of walkers, runners, and cyclists. At the heart of it all is a still, calm lake, reflecting the clouds. This is a place to watch birds, listen for frogs, and see how water, people, and nature share a space. Look for the Environmental Discovery Center for more ways to learn.
  - **What to look for.** Look for the Turtles sunning themselves on the logs in the lake. They stack on top of each other to get the best warm spot!
  - **Good to know.** Restrooms and water are plentiful. The main path is paved and perfect for strollers and bikes. Dogs on leash are welcome. Covered by Regional Parks Pass.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's stand at the edge of the water and be very still for one minute. What do we hear? I hear the lap-lap-lap of the water and the trill of a bird.
  - **A wondering.** I notice the ducks have their heads under the water and their tails up in the air. I wonder what they are looking for down there?
  - **A bit of history.** Spring Lake was made by people, built to help prevent floods.
  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a Tiny Water-Strider Bug who has to skate across the entire big, big lake to deliver a message to a frog on the other side.
  - **Photo.** https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Spring_Lake_Regional_Park_-_December_2022_-_Sarah_Stierch_02.jpg/960px-Spring_Lake_Regional_Park_-_December_2022_-_Sarah_Stierch_02.jpg | Photo by Sarah Stierch, CC BY 4.0 | https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Spring_Lake_Regional_Park_-_December_2022_-_Sarah_Stierch_02.jpg
- [Trione-Annadel State Park](https://parks.ca.gov/?page_id=31891), Santa Rosa. A big, wild park behind Spring Lake with rocky trails, Lake Ilsanjo and fields of wildflowers in spring. Look for buttercups, lupine and poppies on the rocky slopes. What might it feel like to be a fish in Lake Ilsanjo, looking up at the hikers on the shore? *State park, Lake, Wildflowers, Restrooms, Fee.*
  - **A bit about the park.** This is a big, beautiful, and wild park tucked behind Spring Lake. It is famous for its rocky trails, its hidden lake (Lake Ilsanjo), and its incredible fields of wildflowers in the spring. It is a popular place for mountain bikes and long hikes.
  - **What to look for.** Look for wildflowers in the spring. The rocky fields are covered in bright yellow Buttercups, blue Lupine, and vibrant orange Poppies.
  - **Good to know.** This is a State Park, not covered by the Regional Parks Pass. State entry fees apply. Restrooms at the main trailhead. Bring lots of water.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's find a piece of dark, shiny obsidian rock near the trail (but leave it where it is!). Feel how smooth and glassy it is.
  - **A wondering.** I wonder what it feels like to be a fish swimming in Lake Ilsanjo, looking up at all the hikers on the shore?
  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a frog who lives at Lake Ilsanjo and has to find the loudest, deepest croak to win a singing contest with all the other frogs.

- [Taylor Mountain Regional Park and Preserve](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/taylor-mountain-regional-park-and-preserve), Santa Rosa. Hills, grassland and wide views over the city, with trails that climb and little shade. Look for cows grazing and watch how they wrap their tongues around the grass. A hawk circles high above without flapping its wings, so how does it stay up so still? *Regional park, Restrooms, Parks pass.*

  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a Cow who loves her hilltop home but wonders what all those tiny, sparkling lights are in the valley below when the sun goes down.

- [Hood Mountain Regional Park and Preserve](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/hood-mountain-regional-park-and-preserve), Santa Rosa. - [North Sonoma Mountain Regional Park and Preserve](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/north-sonoma-mountain-regional-park-and-preserve), Santa Rosa.   - **A sensory spark.** Let's find a fuzzy, green patch of moss on a rock or a tree trunk. What does it feel like? I think it feels soft and damp.
  - **A wondering.** I notice that some parts of the forest are dark and damp, and some parts are sunny and dry. I wonder what kinds of plants like to live in the shade, and what kinds like the sun?

- [Matanzas Creek Trail](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Matanzas+Creek+Trail+Santa+Rosa), Santa Rosa. A flat, paved path along Matanzas Creek through city neighborhoods, good for strollers, bikes and scooters. Watch for a snowy egret standing still in the water. Plants and vines grow over the creek's concrete walls, so how did those seeds find a home in the middle of the city? *Trail, Birds, Stroller friendly, Free.*

- [Santa Rosa Creek Trail](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/santa-rosa-creek-trail), Santa Rosa. A paved path that follows Santa Rosa Creek across the city, shared with walkers and fast bikes. In fall and winter, look for toyon covered in red berries for the birds. So many people pass by walking, biking and pushing strollers, so where might everyone be going? *Trail, Stroller friendly, Free.*

  - **What to look for.** Look for the Toyon bush, also called Christmas Berry. In the fall and winter, it's covered in bright red berries that the birds love to eat.
  - **Good to know.** This is a flat, paved trail, great for strollers and bikes. It's a "commuter" path, so be aware of fast-moving bicycles. No restrooms. Dogs on leash are welcome. Free access.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's look for "city nature." I see a crow on a street sign and a bright red "berry" bush (Toyon) next to a fence. What city nature can you find?
  - **A wondering.** I notice so many people using this trail. Some are walking, some are biking, some are pushing strollers. I wonder where everyone is going?
  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a speedy, black-and-white Magpie who finds a shiny, lost earring on the trail and has to fly all over the city to find its owner.

- [Colgan Creek Trail](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/colgan-creek-trail), Santa Rosa.   - **A bit about the park.** This is a lovely, neighborhood trail in the southwest part of the city. It's a flat, paved path that is perfect for an easy walk or a first bike ride. It's a quiet place to see wildflowers in the spring and listen to birds in the tall grasses.
  - **What to look for.** Look for the Red-Winged Blackbird. The male is a shiny black bird with bright, fiery red and yellow patches on his wings. You'll hear his "conk-la-REE!" song before you see him.

  - **A bit about the park.** This is a long, flat, paved trail that connects two cities. It's built on an old railroad line, so it's perfectly straight and level. It goes through city neighborhoods, under freeway overpasses, and past wide-open fields and wetlands.

- [Kawana Springs](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Kawana+Springs+Santa+Rosa), Santa Rosa. A short, hilly loop trail on a quiet grassy hill tucked behind a neighborhood.   - **Good to know.** This is a hidden gem. It's a short, hilly loop trail. No restrooms. Dogs on leash are welcome. Free access.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's feel the grass. In the summer, it is dry and golden and crunchy. In the winter, it is wet and green and soft. What does it feel like today?
  - **A wondering.** I notice this park is so quiet. I wonder how many secret, sleeping animals are hiding in the tall grass or in burrows under the ground?

- [Andy's Unity Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/andys-unity-park), Santa Rosa. What might the panels be doing with the sunshine right now? *City park, Playground, Restrooms, Free.*
  - **A bit about the park.** This is a large community park with something for everyone, including a playground, sports fields, a community garden, and a paved path for walking.

  - **A wondering.** I notice this park has solar panels over the parking lot. I wonder how much power they are making from the sun right now?

## North County

- [Foothill Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/foothill-regional-park), Windsor. Shady oak woodland with flat and hilly trails and soft, earthy paths. Listen for acorn woodpeckers and look for trees drilled full of holes and acorns. Acorn caps cover the ground but few acorns, so who is collecting all that food? *Regional park, Birds, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
  - **A bit about the park.** This is a park of Oak Woodlands. It's a quiet, shady place. The ground is dappled with sunlight that comes through the leaves. This is a perfect place to look for acorns, listen for woodpeckers, and walk on soft, earthy trails.
  - **What to look for.** Look for the Acorn Woodpecker. It has a bright red cap and a white face. Listen for its waka-waka call. Look for their "granary" trees, which are tree trunks filled with thousands of holes, each one stuffed with an acorn.
  - **Good to know.** A beautiful park with lots of trail options. Some are flat, some are hilly. Restrooms and water at the trailhead. Dogs on leash are welcome. Covered by Regional Parks Pass.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's find a fallen Bay Laurel leaf and a fallen Oak leaf. Crush them (gently!) in your hand. What does each one smell of? One is spicy, one is earthy.
  - **A wondering.** I notice acorn caps all over the ground, but not as many acorns. I wonder who (or what) is collecting all that food?
  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a Busy Scrub Jay who cannot remember where she buried her most perfect acorn and has to follow a map drawn by a banana slug.
- [Riverfront Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/riverfront-regional-park), Windsor. A flat, easy park beside the Russian River, with lakes made from old gravel pits and tall trees that love water. Watch for a great blue heron standing still at the water's edge. Some trees have white, flaky bark and some have dark, shaggy bark, so why might they be so different? *Regional park, Lake, River, Birds, Stroller friendly, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
  - **A bit about the park.** This park is a hidden secret by the Russian River. It is a flat, easy place to walk, with two beautiful lakes made from old gravel pits. It's a wonderful place for paddling or having a picnic, surrounded by tall trees that love the water.
  - **What to look for.** Look for the Great Blue Heron. This is a very tall, gray-blue bird that stands perfectly still at the edge of the lake, hunting for fish.
  - **Good to know.** This is a flat, easy park, great for strollers and young children. There is a path to the Russian River. Restrooms and water at the trailhead. Dogs on leash are welcome. Covered by Regional Parks Pass.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's look at the surface of the lake. What patterns do the wind and the ducks make in the water? I see ripples and rings.
  - **A wondering.** I notice some of the trees around the lake have white, flaky bark (Sycamores) and some have shaggy, dark bark (Cottonwoods). I wonder why they are so different?
  - **A bit of history.** The two lakes are old gravel pits. People dug out gravel here, and the deep holes filled with water.
  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a Great Blue Heron (the big blue-gray bird) who has to stand perfectly still for a whole hour to try to win a hiding game against a clever fish.
- [Shiloh Ranch Regional Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/shiloh-ranch-regional-park), Windsor. Trails climb through oak woods and grassy meadows to a ridge with big valley views, with little shade on the open paths. In fall and winter, look for toyon with bright red berries. The air feels cooler the moment we step into the shade, so how do the trees do that? *Regional park, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
  - **A bit about the park.** This is a ridge with big views of the valley. The trails climb up through oak woods and grassy meadows. You can feel the sun on the open paths and the cool air in the forest shade. This is a place to see how the land changes as you go higher.
  - **What to look for.** Look for the Toyon bush (also called Christmas Berry). In the fall and winter, it's covered in bright red berries that the birds and coyotes love to eat.
  - **Good to know.** This park has steep trails and little shade. Bring water and be prepared for a climb. Restrooms at the trailhead. Dogs are not allowed in this park. Covered by Regional Parks Pass.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's find a fallen pinecone. What does it feel like? Is it sticky with sap? What does it smell of? It smells sharp and green!
  - **A wondering.** I notice the air feels cooler the moment we walk under the shade of the forest. I wonder how the trees make their own cool air?
  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a Lizard who loves sunbathing on a hot rock but has to play a game of tag with a big tree shadow that keeps trying to cover his spot.
- [Cloverdale River Park](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/cloverdale-river-park), Cloverdale. A peaceful, flat park on the Russian River at the north end of the county, with trees, a boat launch and room for a picnic. Be quiet and you might spot river otters near the banks. The river moves slowly today, so how fast might it run in winter, full of rain? *Regional park, River, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
  - **A bit about the park.** This is a gateway to the Russian River, way up in the north of the county. It’s a peaceful, flat park with beautiful trees and a boat launch. It’s a perfect place to see the river, have a picnic, and listen to the birds.
  - **What to look for.** Look for River Otters! You have to be quiet and lucky, but you might see them playing in the water near the banks, or sliding down a muddy slide.
  - **Good to know.** A beautiful, flat park, great for an easy walk. Restrooms and water are available. Dogs on leash are welcome. Covered by Regional Parks Pass.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's find a smooth, flat river rock. How many can you find? I like the gray ones and the green ones. How does it feel in your hand compared to a rough rock from the trail?
  - **A wondering.** I notice the river is moving so slowly today. I wonder how fast it moves in the winter when it is full of rain?
  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a Little Salmon who is swimming all the way from the ocean and is trying to find the exact creek where he was born.
- [Healdsburg Veterans Memorial Beach](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/healdsburg-veterans-memorial-beach), Healdsburg. A sunny summer beach on the Russian River, with shady picnic spots under the trees. Look up at the tall trees that shade the picnic area. Here the river is an open swimming beach, and at other parks it is wild and fast, so how many different moods does the river have? *Regional park, River, Beach, Restrooms, Parks pass.*
  - **A bit about the park.** This is a classic summer park, a sunny beach on the Russian River. It’s a place to wade in the water, build a sandcastle on the shore, and have a shady picnic under the redwood trees. It's a place for cool water on a hot day.
  - **What to look for.** Look for the Redwood Trees that give shade to the picnic area. These are coastal redwoods, living right next to the river.
  - **Good to know.** This is a summer "swimming" beach. The dam is usually up from July to September. Restrooms and changing rooms are available. Dogs on leash are welcome. Covered by Regional Parks Pass.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's sit at the edge of the river. Is the water cold? Is the sand hot? I notice the small, quick minnows swimming by our feet in the clear water.
  - **A wondering.** I notice the river here is a big, open swimming beach, but at other parks it's a wild, fast-moving place. I wonder how many different "personalities" the river has?
  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a Dragonfly who loves to zoom over the river and challenge the little minnows to a race from one side of the beach to the other.
  - **Photo.** https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Healdsburg_Municipal_Beach_postcard.jpg/960px-Healdsburg_Municipal_Beach_postcard.jpg | Postcard, public domain | https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Healdsburg_Municipal_Beach_postcard.jpg
- [Del Rio Woods](https://parks.sonomacounty.ca.gov/visit/find-a-park/del-rio-woods), Healdsburg. A shady park on the Russian River with tall redwood, fir and oak trees, a beach and a gentle trail. Look for redwood sorrel, a clover-shaped plant carpeting the forest floor. Redwood bark is deep and stringy and bay bark is smooth and gray, so why might they be so different? *Regional park, River, Redwoods, Restrooms, Free.*
  - **A bit about the park.** This is a beautiful, shady park on the Russian River, full of tall redwood, fir, and oak trees. It has a lovely beach and a trail that is perfect for a gentle walk. It feels hidden and quiet.
  - **What to look for.** Look for Redwood Sorrel. It's a beautiful plant with clover-shaped leaves that carpets the forest floor. We look and leave it growing.
  - **Good to know.** This park has a lovely, flat trail. Restrooms are available. Dogs on leash are welcome. Free access.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's find a soft, green sorrel or clover leaf on the forest floor. What does it feel like? What does it smell of? It smells green and fresh.
  - **A wondering.** I notice the redwood trees have deep, rough, stringy bark. I wonder why their bark is so different from the smooth, gray bark of the bay trees?
  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a family of squirrels who live in the tallest fir tree and have a competition to see who can gather the most acorns and pinecones.
- [Russian River beaches](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Russian+River+beaches+Russian+River+area), Russian River area. Small access points along the Russian River, often with a little beach or a place to launch a canoe. Look for dragonflies with shiny bodies and clear wings hunting near the water. How many little beaches line the river, and how many could we visit in one day? *River, Beach, Free.*
  - **A bit about the park.** This isn't just one park, but many small "access" points to the Russian River. These are spots where you can get to the water, often with a small beach or a place to launch a canoe.
  - **What to look for.** Look for Dragonflies. These amazing, fast-flying insects have shiny, colorful bodies and clear wings. They love to hunt for mosquitoes near the water.
  - **Good to know.** These are small, simple access points. Most do not have restrooms. Dogs on leash are welcome. Free access.
  - **A sensory spark.** Let's find a smooth, flat river rock. What does it feel like in your hand? Is it warm from the sun?
  - **A wondering.** I wonder how many of these little beaches there are? I wonder if we could visit all of them in one day?
  - **A story spark.** Tell a story about a river otter who knows all the secret, hidden beaches and has a favorite one for napping, a favorite one for sliding, and a favorite one for eating.
